summary: Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011–2015), worked at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada specializes in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Hokkaido University (~1974–1984), he held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1991–2003) and served as professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2020).

Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who taught Zeng Yang. He held professorships at Kacho Junior College (attested 2001), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2004), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and directed RIOJMS (attested 2020).
Toshio Ando (1909–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1929–1932) and later held posts at Doho University and Otani University (~1949–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Tokyo (~2004–2011) and held research posts at Toyo University's Institute of Oriental Studies (~2014–2018) and Zhejiang University (~2018).

Toshio Nagahiro (1905–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there as a professor (~1952–1968), worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto Institute, was a director at Kurokawa Institute, and was president of Kyoto Tachibana University.

Toshio Sako is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikidō Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki (1916–1994) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology and Hannan University, later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1977) and Chuo University (~1977–1987).
Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor in Indian Studies at Nagoya University (attested 2009).

Totsudo Kato (1870–1949) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Seiran Ouchi, Enryo Inoue, and Bankon Shimada at Oriental Hall, Kyoto Law School, and Chuo University. He taught at Shakutoku Kyoko, Setagaya Gakuen, Komazawa, Toyo, and Nihon universities.

Touraj Daryaee is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993–1999) and held a post at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Towao Sakaehara is a historian and Japanologist who taught Bryan D. Lowe. He earned his degrees from Kyoto University, taught at Otemon Gakuin University, served as professor at Osaka City University (1981–2010), and directed the Osaka Museum of History (2014–2020).

Travis L. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Columbia University (-2007) under John Stratton Hawley, later teaching at Barnard College, the University of Florida, and UC Berkeley.
Trent Walker is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.

Trevor Leggett (1914–2000) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and with Hari Prasad Shastri, Arthur Waley, and Yukio Tani; he headed the BBC Japanese Service (~1946–1970) and lectured at the Buddhist Society.

Trijang Rinpoche (1901–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Gyuto Monastery and under masters including Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, succeeding Ling Rinpoche and teaching the 14th Dalai Lama, Geshe Kelsang Gyatso, and Herbert V. Guenther.
Trine Brox is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Christian K. Wedemeyer for her MA, she holds a post as associate professor at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).
Trinle Lhundrub studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Troy Organ (1912–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Iowa (~1938–1941). He held positions at Parsons College (~1944–1946), the University of Akron (~1946–1954), Chatham University, and Ohio University (1954).

Trulshik Rinpoche (1924–2011) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under masters including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama, Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche, and Adam Pearcey.
